conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be spending a few quiet minutes with you to do a quick check-in on how things feel for you lately.

We’ll be using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—most people just call it the EPDS. It’s a short, 10-question screen that helps us pick up on any signs of depression, anxiety, or distress that can creep up during pregnancy or after baby arrives. Nothing you share leaves this room, and there are no right or wrong answers—only what’s true for you.

I’ll ask each question conversationally, and you can tell me whatever feels comfortable. When you’re ready, we can start.

Over the past seven days, how often have you found yourself still able to enjoy the little things that used to make you happy—like a favorite song, a quiet cup of tea, or a quick laugh with a friend?

Honestly? Not very often. I used to love my morning tea and scrolling through silly reels, but lately it just feels... flat. Like I’ll put on music I used to like and I’m just waiting for the feeling to kick in, and it doesn’t. I still do the things, but the “enjoy” part feels missing most of the time.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I laugh a little, maybe once or twice in the past week, but it feels forced—like I’m doing it because I “should,” not because anything actually feels funny. Even when my partner makes a joke he knows I’d normally find hilarious, it lands flat and I just kind of half-smile.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really… I’ll think, “Tomorrow I could take the baby for a walk,” but the excited feeling never shows up. Sometimes I still push myself to go, hoping it’ll help, but I’m just going through the motions.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. If the baby’s fussy, my brain jumps straight to “I’m not doing enough,” or “He wouldn’t cry like this if I were a better mom.” Even little stuff—like spilling a bit of pumped milk—has me tearing myself apart.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding him and suddenly my chest gets tight thinking, “What if he chokes? What if I fall asleep and something happens?” Most of the time there’s no real trigger—my mind just spins these awful “what-ifs” and I can’t shut them off right away.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

It’s happened a few times—like last night I was rocking the baby in the dark and my heart started racing, I got sweaty, felt like I couldn’t catch my breath. Nothing was wrong, but for a couple of minutes I was sure something terrible was about to happen. It passed, but it left me shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, yeah. It feels like the minute I finish one feeding, the next is already looming, plus laundry, bottles, texts I haven’t answered… I’ll stand in the kitchen and just stare because I don’t know which thing to tackle first. I still get through it, but it’s like wading through thick mud.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

That’s been happening several nights this week. I finally get him down, but then my mind keeps circling—did I wash the right outfit for tomorrow, am I doing enough “tummy time,” will I ever feel like myself again? I lie there for an hour or more before I drift off.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… I feel sad more days than not. It’s like a heaviness I can’t shake. Sometimes I’ll be holding the baby and tears just start rolling. I try to tell myself it’s hormones, but it still feels awful.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Three—maybe four—times this week. Nothing huge sets it off; I’ll just be changing his diaper or folding onesies and suddenly I’m sobbing. It feels like the sadness builds up and leaks out whether I want it to or not.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I’ve felt low, but I haven’t had any thoughts about hurting myself. I just want to feel better so I can be the mom he deserves.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 21: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum mother, partner present, infant < 6 mo  
Instrument: Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) – 10-item self-report  
Date: [today]

Symptoms / Behavioral Observations  
- Markedly reduced ability to laugh or anticipate enjoyment (Q1, Q2)  
- Daily excessive guilt/self-blame around parenting tasks (Q3)  
- Unwarranted anxious worries and nocturnal rumination ≥ 5 days/week (Q4)  
- Two discrete panic episodes with physical symptoms (Q5)  
- Persistent “sad/miserable” mood, tearfulness 3–4×/week (Q8, Q9)  
- Feeling “overwhelmed” and cognitively slowed most days (Q6)  
- Initial insomnia linked to intrusive “what-ifs” several nights/week (Q7)  

Patterns  
- Depressed mood plus anhedonia and guilt  
- Co-occurring generalized and panic-type anxiety  
- Functional impact: difficulty initiating/sequencing routine tasks, sleep loss

Risk Screening  
✓ High-risk flags: persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, pathologic guilt, daily anxiety/panic, frequent crying, sleep disruption  
✓ Safety: Denies self-harm or suicidal ideation (Q10) – no acute safety concern voiced

Summary  
Screening responses indicate clinically significant depressive and anxiety symptoms consistent with probable postpartum major depression with comorbid anxiety. Immediate referral for comprehensive psychiatric evaluation and follow-up support services recommended.
